_comment: Canonical genre/mood/geography/attribute vocabulary for genre aggregation.
This file is the SHIPPED DEFAULT. A user's edits from the Config page are written
to <config_dir>/genre_vocabulary.json and take precedence, so a repo update never
clobbers them. The Config page offers a reset back to this file.
Entry shape:
id           stable canonical identity, never a display string (snake_case)
display      what gets written to the file tags
parent       id of the immediate broader genre, or null for a family root
parents      list form for hybrids; the FIRST parent is the primary lineage
specificity  0 family root, 1 broad, 2 established subgenre, 3 narrow/microgenre
(a child is never less specific than any of its parents)
aliases      EXTRA spellings only - the lowercased display name and the
id-with-spaces are derived automatically, so do not repeat them
family       hierarchy branch used for the family-slot limit; defaults to the
root ancestor's id when omitted. Hybrids always set it explicitly.
scope        OPTIONAL. Which evidence levels may create this genre and whether it
takes a genre slot. Omitted = evidence_policy.default_scope.
levels                       track / album / artist
slot                         'genre' (default) or 'marker' (never uses a slot)
confirm_release_types        MusicBrainz release-group secondary types
confirm_album_title_patterns regex against the album title
confirm_title_patterns       regex against the track title
require_confirmation         true = rejected unless a confirm rule matches
artist_requires_min_sources  artist evidence counts only with N source groups
redundant_with OPTIONAL (v5). If ANY listed genre is also selected for the track, this
genre is dropped. Applied after slot selection; the freed slot is not
refilled; never empties a track. An explicit keep_together pair wins.
v4 notes:
'hardcore' is METALLIC hardcore (Hatebreed-style); 'hardcore_punk' is the punk lineage;
'hardcore rap' / 'hardcore hip hop' resolve to Hardcore Hip-Hop, never to Hardcore.
Soundtrack / Film Score / Video Game Music need a soundtrack release; artist evidence never counts.
Christmas / Soundtrack / Comedy are markers and never use a Maximum Genres slot.
Discogs 'Folk, World, & Country' must be read as ONE value, not split on commas.
'noise_values' are dropped outright (chart artefacts, vocal descriptors).
v5 notes (A -> Stray Kids audit, report 15):
Added aliases for common unmapped source values and 7 noise values.
Added redundant_with lists (Heavy Metal vs specific metal styles, Rap Metal vs Nu Metal,
broad rock/pop vs specific punk styles, etc). Classic Rock is deliberately NOT redundant.
Alternative Metal + Nu Metal is NOT redundant (kept together by design).
evidence_policy.collection_policy holds the new selection rules.
Adding an entry is enough to make it selectable; nothing is hardcoded in Python.
How a composite source value is split into genres.
hard_delimiters: always separate genres; split FIRST, before any whole-value match.
soft_joiners: separate genres in a list ("Funk / Soul") but also occur INSIDE
real names (death/doom, r&b, drum & bass), so the whole value is tried first.
protected_values: real names that contain a hard delimiter. Matched whole BEFORE
splitting, so "Folk, World, & Country" stays one genre.

aliases: new wave of british heavy metal

_comment: Adjective -> country. Applied ONLY to values that are not a recognised genre,
so 'K-pop' / 'Britpop' / 'Americana' / 'Neue Deutsche Härte' stay genres.
Bare country NAMES are listed too, because a source may supply either form
('Norway' or 'Norwegian'). A name that is ALSO a genre still resolves to the
genre, because genre is classified first.
Performance/recording attributes - never genre slots. is_* booleans on the tracks
table remain the authoritative store.
Values that are never genres, moods, places or attributes. Matched exactly
(lowercased) and dropped before scoring. Decades are caught by the junk filter.
How genre evidence becomes a score, and what each Final Genre position requires.
evidence = provider_trust x level_weight x tag_dilution; a genre's score is the sum over
sources, then x corroboration. Per-genre 'scope' is applied BEFORE scoring.
Provider trust itself stays in config (Provider Trust panel) - it is not duplicated here.

source_levels._comment: Level a provider's evidence represents when the provider does not report one.

source_groups._comment: Sources in one group count as ONE voice for corroboration (ListenBrainz genres derive from MusicBrainz).

artist_only._comment: A genre backed ONLY by artist-level evidence may fill position 1 for a track with no other evidence, never more.

tag_dilution._comment: When one source lists more than 'threshold' tags for a track, each is weighted sqrt(threshold/n).

hybrid_support._comment: A multi-parent genre needs direct evidence above this score, or support in at least this many of its parents' families.

markers._comment: Genres with scope.slot = 'marker' are written on top of the selected genres and never take a slot.

_comment: v5 selection rules, applied in this order after scoring and outlier rejection:
1. metal_rock_arbitration: symmetric. Share = metal / (metal + rock) over rival candidates,
using trust x level x corroboration ONLY (no tag-position weighting), roots excluded.
share >= metal_wins_at -> drop rock family; share <= rock_wins_at -> drop metal family;
between the two -> keep both. Same-sound pairs (e.g. Gothic Rock + Gothic Metal, both selected)
are not arbitrated: the metal name wins. Crossover companions (Nu/Alt Metal + Hard Rock) still apply.
2. root_fallback_only: specificity-0 genres are excluded from the pool and the relative-floor
reference whenever a non-root candidate scores >= position 1 min_score.
3. restore_parent_if_empty: if ancestor condensing leaves nothing passing position 1, re-select
without condensing.
4. position3_new_family: position 3 may accept 1 source group when the genre is named by BOTH
MusicBrainz and ListenBrainz at track level and its family is not already in positions 1-2.
5. artist_only_same_family: artist-only evidence may only add a genre whose family already
appears in track/album evidence.
6. redundant_genres: apply each genre's redundant_with after selection; no refill; never empty;
explicit keep_together pairs always win.

root_fallback_only._comment: Drop a specificity-0 genre only when a more specific genre from the SAME family is selected (Rock + Hard Rock -> Hard Rock). Punk next to Hard Rock is kept.
